statements.text: To assert something one must believe it, so to assert eliminative materialism the eliminativist must believe it, and then there are beliefs and the view is false. Boghossian presses a subtler version: arguments against the content of attitudes apply to all content, and irrealism about content presupposes realist notions of truth and reference.

sources.quote: But if the eliminativist has such a belief, then there are beliefs and eliminativism is thereby proven false.
there are no truth conditions and yet certain sentences (or beliefs) about content are false
